scope.evidence_basis: Author expansion and rereading of the displayed square identity, both positivity directions, congruence computation and scalar failure model.

N-main: Use the exact square identity to isolate the residual form.
Use the invertible change of variables for sufficiency.
Choose x=-A^{-1}By for every nonzero y to prove necessity.
Compare congruence and minimization under their actual common hypotheses.
Expand the square with A symmetric and invertible.

N-main.objects: Real symmetric blocks with all sizes declared; positivity means the quadratic form on every nonzero vector.
N-main.domain: Integers p,q>=1, A p by p, B p by q, C q by q are retained.
N-main.fixed_and_variable: A,B,C are fixed arbitrary blocks; test vectors x,y vary over their full real spaces.
N-main.hypotheses: A is symmetric strictly positive definite, not merely invertible; C is symmetric and B has the matching sizes.
N-main.equations: M and S=C-B^T A^{-1}B are displayed inside the canonical theorem.
N-main.quantifiers: Both directions hold for every admissible choice of blocks; positivity quantifies every nonzero vector, not a single test.
N-main.conclusion: Precisely M>0 iff S>0 under the stated A>0 assumption; no singular or semidefinite extension is stated.
N-main.status: Known classical theorem with the elementary proof expanded here, never an originality assertion.
N-main.local_definitions: Positive definite is defined in the canonical statement; ordinary transpose and inverse belong to the declared linear-algebra baseline.
